annotations.title: Prieſt.
annotations.text: The Prieſts of the old law (ſaith S. Chryſoſtome) had authoritie and priuilege only to diſcerne who where healed of leproſie, and to denounce the ſame to the people: but the Prieſts of the new law haue power to purge in very deede the filth of the ſoule. ◦Therfore whoſoeuer deſpiſeth them, is more vvorthie to be puniſhed then the rebel Dathan and his complices. S. Chryſo. li. 3. de Sacerd.

annotations.title: Gift.
annotations.text: Our Sauiour willeth him to goe and offer his gift or ſacrifice according as Moyſes preſcribed in that caſe, becauſe the other ſacrifice being the holieſt of al holies, which is his body, was not yet begonne. So ſaith S. Aug. li. 2. q. Euang. q. 3. & Cont. Aduers. leg. & Proph. li. 1. c. 19. 20.

annotations.title: Not worthy.
annotations.text: Orig. ho. 5. in diuers. When thou eateſt (ſaith he) and drinkeſt the body and bloud of our Lord, he entereth vnder thy roofe. Thou alſo therfore humbling thy ſelf, ſay: [1] Lord I am not worthy. &c. So ſaid [2] S. Chryſoſtom in his Maſſe. and ſo doeth the Cath. Churche vſe at this day in euery Maſſe. See S. Auguſtine ep. 118 ad Ianu.

annotations.title: His wiues mother.
annotations.text: [1] Of Peter ſpecially among the reſt it is euident that he had a wife, but (as S. Hierom ſayth) after they were called to be Apoſtles, they had no more carnal companie with their wiues, as he proueth there by the very wordes of our Sauiour, [2] He that hath left wife &c. And ſo in the Latin Churche hath been alwayes vſed, that maried men may be and are daily made Prieſts, either after the death of the wife, or with her conſent to liue in perpetual continencie. And if the Greekes haue Prieſts that doe otherwiſe, S. Epiphanius a Greeke Doctor telleth them that they doe it agaynſt the ancient Canons, and [3] Paphnutius plainely ſignifieth the ſame in the firſt Councel of Nice. But this is moſt playne, that there was neuer either in the Greeke Church or the Latin, authentical example of any that married after holy Orders.

notes.text: Lib. 1. adv. Iov. C. 14. Mt. 19, 29. Epiph. hæ. 59.

annotations.title: Let the dead.
annotations.text: By this we ſee that not only no wordly or carnal reſpect, but no other laudable dutie toward our parents, ought to ſtay vs from folowing Chriſt, and chooſing a life of greater perfection.

annotations.title: He commaunded.
annotations.text: The Churche (here ſignified by the boate or ſhippe) and Catholikes, are often toſſed with ſtormes of perſecution, but Chriſt who ſeemed to ſleepe in the meane time, by the Churches prayers awaketh, and maketh a calme.
